question.:question/problem:
What are the pivot columns of the matrix $A,$ given by

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 8 & -6 \\ 0 & -2 & -4 & 1 \\ 1 & 4 & 0 & 2\end{bmatrix}?
$$

Select all that apply.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we need to convert $A$ to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 8 & -6 \\ 0 & -2 & -4 & 1 \\ 1 & 4 & 0 & 2\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{4} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 4 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 8 & -6 \\ 0 & -2 & -4 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 4 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 8 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that $A$ has $3$ pivots. In particular, the pivot columns are the $1$st, $2$nd, and $4$th columns.
